children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets: ** South Korean shares logged a second weekly decline as the AI optimism following Nvidia's outlook waned while investors stayed cautious ahead of the Federal Reserve's Jackson Hole event. The won strengthened to the strongest level against the dollar since July 2025, while the benchmark bond yield rose. ** The benchmark KOSPI
closed down 123.49 points, or 1.79%, at 6,788.88. For the week, the index declined 1.79%. ** Among index heavyweights, chipmaker Samsung Electronics
lost 4.45%. Battery maker LG Energy Solution
** Nvidia's second-quarter revenue more than doubled to $96.22 billion, beating estimates of $92.17 billion.

** Federal Reserve officials shared on Thursday their ongoing concerns about the U.S. inflation landscape, as central bankers gathered in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, for the Kansas City Fed's closely watched annual economic symposium.      ** Hyundai Motor
were up 0.38% and 1.51%, respectively. Steelmaker POSCO Holdings
fell 6.78%. ** Of the total 910 traded issues, 640 shares advanced, while 238 declined. ** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 1,756.4 billion won. ** In offshore trading, the won

was quoted at 1,373.3 per dollar, up 0.6% on the day, while in non-deliverable forward trading its one-month contract (KRW1MNDFOR=) was quoted at 1,372.9. ** The KOSPI has risen 61.10% so far this year. ** The won has strengthened 4.9% against the dollar so far this year. ** In money and debt markets, September futures on three-year treasury bonds (KTBc1) lost 0.17 point to 103.34. ** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) rose by 4.4 basis points to 3.798%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
